target_customer: Internet businesses and developers who need to accept online payments, later platforms and enterprises
problem: Accepting card payments online required a merchant account, a gateway contract and clumsy integrations, which took days or weeks for a developer.
business_model: usage-based payments API with a percentage plus fixed fee per transaction, plus add-on products

founders.name: Patrick Collison
founders.background_notes: Irish; Wikipedia gives founding as 2010 in Palo Alto

competitors.name: Authorize.net
competitors.what: incumbent payment gateway needing a separate merchant account
competitors.funding_then: owned by CyberSource, bought by Visa in 2010

competitors.name: PayPal
competitors.what: consumer-trusted payments with a complex merchant setup

competitors.name: Braintree
competitors.what: developer-friendlier gateway still needing merchant application

technical_complexity.rationale: Hard parts were bank and card network integrations, fraud and compliance, and building a clean API on top of legacy rails with a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Early copying was feasible but bank relationships, compliance, developer mindshare and integrations compounded over time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: PayPal bought Braintree in 2013 for $800M but Stripe kept growing and stayed independent.

market_need_then: Developers complained that online payment setup was slow and opaque; e-commerce and SaaS were growing and incumbents had poor developer experience.

branding.name_origin: Started as /dev/payments, which failed on Delaware incorporation rules, so the founders picked a new name; PayDemon was considered. One weak source links Stripe to the card magnetic stripe, unverified.
branding.domain_note: Bought stripe.com from its owner around 2011, price reported as tens of thousands of dollars by one source and undisclosed by another

identity.logo: lowercase or wordmark in a purple-blue palette
identity.visual_style: clean developer-oriented design with polished documentation

branding.brand_signature: Highly regarded API documentation and developer experience
branding.community_and_virality: Developers praised its documentation and the seven-line integration online, spreading adoption by word of mouth.

brand_strength.rationale: Became synonymous with developer-first payments; sources emphasize developer trust, but evidence is mostly secondary blogs.

outcome_analysis: Stripe won by making payment acceptance a few lines of code against slow incumbents while e-commerce and SaaS grew. It raised from top investors early, stayed independent when rival Braintree was bought, and by 2025 and 2026 offered employee tenders at valuations of $91.5B and then $159B instead of going public.
notes: Series A reported by aggregators as $18M at $100M valuation, Series B $20M July 2012 led by General Catalyst, Series C $80M Jan 2014 at $1.75B: all single-source or aggregator, unverified so not recorded as rounds. Seed date conflicts (March vs May 2011). Valuations 2021 $95B, 2023 $50B, tenders 2025 $91.5B and 2026 $159B are secondary or tender events. Wikipedia infobox says 2009 while body says 2010. Founder education and Auctomatic from general knowledge, not fetched in this run.
